answerCheck.derivedAnswer: A. The normal vectors of the two planes.
answerCheck.reason: Two planes are perpendicular exactly when their normal vectors are perpendicular. Arbitrary directions within the planes do not provide this criterion.
Normal vectors are nonzero, so their zero dot product means they are perpendicular. The corresponding planes are therefore perpendicular.
The square gives AD=AB=5. Since AD is perpendicular to plane PAB, angle PAD is right, and PD²=PA²+AD²=3²+5²=34.
Parallel or coincident planes have collinear normals. Noncollinear normals exclude both possibilities, so the planes intersect in a line.
